target.status: Met on the representative edit with prepared 540p seek cache; uncovered-source fallback remains above target
target.scope: After preview session preparation; report cold, resident, and cached requests separately; exact selected frame on release; latest request wins

original.definition: Request to exact source-frame callback for every visible video plus one animation frame after preview/graphics readiness. Excludes session preparation; not physical scanout. readyMs is sampled at animation cadence.

intraframeControl.definition: Request to exact source-frame callback for every visible video plus one animation frame after preview/graphics readiness. Excludes session preparation; not physical scanout. readyMs is sampled at animation cadence.
intraframeControl.scope: Only the first source was replaced with a 12-second full-resolution 2560x1440 H.264 all-I control. Distant-seek results mix original and control sources and are not an all-intra benchmark. Audio is disabled for that control source; seeking is paused.
intraframeControl.encoding: FFmpeg D3D11VA input, h264_nvenc p1, tune ll, constqp 18, g=1, bf=0, original frame rate and dimensions

interpretation: Native distant seeking is faster than the older 390-766 ms software/compositor measurements, but adjacent frame stepping is slower. Original-video position() dominates the measured work. Changing only first-source encoding reduces resident forward/backward/nearby latency to around 36-38 ms. Proxies alone have not established 25 ms. No continuous scrub performance claim is made by this isolated-seek diagnostic.
nextStep: Bounded decoded-frame cache and seek-friendly media, with a continuous latest-request scrub measurement. Keep original media for export and preserve exact timestamp selection.

sources.relevance: Dragging uses the animation budget, about 16.7 ms per frame at 60 Hz. 50 ms input-handler guidance explicitly excludes dragging.
Current benchmark uses export/Null Encoder processing, not a published click-to-picture seek latency.
Premiere supports proxy media for editing performance.
Final Cut supports ProRes optimized media for editing performance.

preparedSeekCache.definition: Request to the next animation frame after exact visible source-frame and preview/graphic readiness. Event-driven readiness avoids the old diagnostic polling an extra animation frame. Excludes session preparation; not physical scanout.
